requirement:
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.excerpts`. I did not request implementation source. The judgment rests on the supplied test text only.

**Obligations derived from the text:**
1. Every `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` excerpt, matching and context lines alike, is clipped to the source span of the outline item named by `file` and `item`.
2. That span includes the item's attached source under `requirements.references.outline_comments`. This covers leading doc comments, attributes, and a trailing comment that follows other source on the same line.
3. Clipping applies within a line that different items share.

**Mapping to tests:**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_excerpts_stop_at_byte_boundaries_including_attached_comments_and_attributes]` runs both `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` against one fixture. `ripgrep` uses `context: 99`, so context would spill into neighbouring items if clipping failed.
  - Context clipping: the assertions check that `unwanted_before`, `unwanted_after`, `unwanted_last` and `fn last` never appear in any result, which rules out unclipped context.
  - Attached leading source: `ripgrep` results for `fn[target]` must contain `needle docs` (the doc comment) and `#[inline]` (the attribute). A separate `inline` search returns exactly `fn[target]` and `fn[right]`.
  - Shared line: the line `fn left() {...} /* needle attached */ #[inline] fn right() {...} fn last() {...}` holds three items. Both tools must return `fn[left]` and `fn[right]` as separate matches.
    - The `fn[left]` excerpt must contain `needle attached` and not `fn right`. This also checks that a trailing comment on a shared line belongs to the earlier item.
    - The `fn[right]` excerpt must contain `#[inline] fn right` but not `fn left` or `needle attached`. It must also exclude `fn last`.
  - Byte boundaries: the multi-byte `café` is matched on its own with `context: 0`, which checks clipping at byte offsets.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[exact_match_ranges_preserve_regex_anchors_and_skip_unmatched_or_binary_sources]` covers anchored regexes (`^`, `$`) and a case-insensitive pattern with `context: 10`. It asserts that the `lines` array is exactly the single matched line `fn exact() { needle(); }`. This confirms that clipping does not distort match ranges and that context from other items is excluded.

**Gaps considered:**
- Only Rust fixtures are used. The text sets one clipping rule for every excerpt and does not distinguish languages, so I did not treat this as a gap.
- I did not find an `ast_grep` case where a multi-line match crosses item boundaries. The text does not single that case out.

Both modes, the attached-source rule and the shared-line rule each have a test with assertions that enforce the expected outcome.

text: :::{req} search_accounting.excerpts
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
